title: Integration by Parts: Accumulating ∫ x·eˣ dx
caption_md: The shaded area shows $F(x) = \int_0^x t\,e^t\,dt$ as you drag $x$ to the right. Integration by parts tells us this equals $x\,e^x - e^x + 1$. Drag the upper bound and watch the accumulated area grow. Notice how the integrand $t\,e^t$ is negative for $t<0$ (the product of a negative algebraic piece and a small exponential) and positive for $t>0$, so the area dips before climbing steeply — confirming why we need a technique like by-parts to antidifferentiate products.
